title: Orsen and the Spire
premise: Jude Halloran, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a smuggler in the Thornfell mountains, discovers her own name and tonight's date in a century-old prophecy book that predicts she will either destroy or save the Spire—the seat of the mage order that exiled her. Hunted by the Spire's inquisitors and shadowed by her loyal partner Kess, who doesn't know what Jude is, Jude races to find the prophecy's author and learns the truth: the Spire's power is fed by imprisoned storm-spirits, and her exile was engineered to breed a weapon. In the climax at the Spire, Jude must choose between freeing the spirits—which would shatter the wards protecting the realm—and preserving the corrupt order that made her; she frees them, takes the storms into herself, and vanishes into legend, leaving Kess to carry the truth.
about_author: Ada Marchetti is the pen name of a former mountain guide turned novelist who writes fantasy rooted in weather, borders, and the people who live outside them. She lives in a stone farmhouse where the power goes out often enough to keep her honest.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Almanac
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She guides contraband through Thornfell passes with Kess, dodging Spire patrols, establishing her careful invisibility and wry voice. Emotional beat: restless contentment built on buried fear—she hasn't called a storm in seven years.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Grief
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A dying book-hoarder client pays her in volumes instead of coin; one is a prophecy book written a century ago. She finds tonight's date, her true name, and two divergent endings. Emotional beat: cold vertigo.

chapters.title: What Kess Doesn't Know
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. He notices Jude unraveling and covers for her with their fence, revealing his own debts and fierce loyalty. Emotional beat: love expressed as protection, and the first crack of doubt about his partner.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Spire inquisitor Vael Corrane arrives in the valley town asking after a storm-caller born under a black moon. Jude realizes the prophecy has readers on both sides. Emotional beat: hunted stillness.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Jude's POV. Her trial and exile: the Spire branded her magic heretical, but fragments suggest her sentence was scripted. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Road to Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Jude and Kess's POV alternating. They flee along smuggler roads toward the dead monastery where the prophet lived, pursued by Corrane. Emotional beat: trust deepening under pressure, lies accumulating.

chapters.title: Ash and Marginalia
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In Hollowmere's ruins she finds the prophet's annotations: the Spire feeds on caged storm-spirits, and 'the Halloran girl' was bred for release or ruin. Emotional beat: horror reframing her whole life.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Lightning
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ambushed by bounty mages, Jude breaks her silence and calls a storm to save Kess—her first in seven years. Emotional beat: exhilaration and terror; there is no going back.

chapters.title: Corrane's Offer
chapters.summary: Vael Corrane's POV. The inquisitor captures Kess and offers Jude amnesty if she surrenders before the dark moon. His chapters reveal he believes he's saving the realm. Emotional beat: sincere fanaticism.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Blackmoon Ford
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude trades herself for Kess, lying that she'll comply, and slips the Spire's binding collar with a trick from her exile years. Emotional beat: sacrifice braided with deception.

chapters.title: Kess Learns the Truth
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Freed but abandoned, Kess finds the prophecy book Jude left behind and reads her name in it. Emotional beat: betrayal, then resolve—he goes after her anyway.

chapters.title: The Spirit Roads
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Guided by the prophet's map, Jude descends beneath Thornfell into the spirit roads where caged storms whisper her name—they know her, and call her daughter. Emotional beat: uncanny belonging.

chapters.title: The Author's Grave
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the prophet's tomb she learns the final truth: the prophet was her ancestor, and every 'choice' in the prophecy was a cage of another kind. Emotional beat: fury at being written.

chapters.title: Council of Storms
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The freed spirits convene within Jude's dreams, offering power at the price of carrying them—and the war they remember. Emotional beat: awe and dread entwined.

chapters.title: The Spire Ascendant
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. Kess infiltrates the Spire as a laborer, mapping its wards, discovering the Archmage plans to drain a new spirit at the dark moon rite. Emotional beat: ordinary courage against vast machinery.

chapters.title: Collar and Crown
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Recaptured by Corrane, Jude is brought to the Spire in chains—as the rite's intended vessel. She and Kess nearly cross paths in the corridors. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread.

chapters.title: The Dark Moon Rite
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The rite begins; the Archmage reveals the ancient war was started by the Spire itself to justify its prisons. Jude's bindings fail as the storms answer her. Emotional beat: revelation as detonation.

chapters.title: Every Road Burns
chapters.summary: Climax part one, Jude's POV. Battle through the Spire as wards collapse; Corrane, shown the truth in the storm's memory, turns his blade on the Archmage. Emotional beat: enemy becoming ally too late.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Halloran Girl
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Jude's POV. At the spirit-cage heart, Jude chooses the third path the prophecy never wrote: she takes the storms into her own body rather than loose them unbound. Emotional beat: self-authorship at terrible cost.

chapters.title: After the Weather
chapters.summary: Kess's POV. The Spire stands broken, the realm's wards fraying but holding; Kess searches the ruins and finds only scorched footprints walking into Thornfell. Emotional beat: mourning without a grave.

chapters.title: The New Almanac
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Kess's POV. Months later, Kess runs the passes alone, telling travelers stories of a woman made of weather. On the highest ridge, lightning answers when he speaks her name. Emotional beat: hope as open road.

chapters.title: Storm-Caller, Still Walking
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Jude's POV. Far beyond the maps, Jude—part storm, part woman—chooses each day who she is now, writing her own almanac in rain and quiet. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, identity claimed.
